name: Podcast Intelligence
summary: Turn podcast episodes and media files into transcripts, summaries and searchable answers.
intro: Import local media or resolve podcast links, then explore timestamped transcripts and summaries. Ask questions with citations that return you to the source audio.

features.title: Flexible import
features.body: Import audio/video files, media URLs and podcasts through RSS or supported directory links.

features.title: Timestamped understanding
features.body: Reuse published transcripts or configure transcription, summaries and speaker-aware processing.

features.title: Grounded questions
features.body: Search episode content and follow answer citations to playback positions.

features.title: Export and integration
features.body: Export JSON, Markdown, SRT or VTT and optionally connect compatible clients through MCP.

support.title: Set up processing
paragraphs: Choose providers in desktop settings. The default demo profile supplies demonstration behavior; configure suitable transcription, embedding and language-model providers for real processing.

support.title: Import problems
paragraphs: Confirm that a URL resolves to accessible public media or RSS. Protected, unsupported, oversized or unsafe download destinations may be rejected.

support.title: Provider problems
paragraphs: Check the endpoint, API key, model and supported audio or embedding options. Save settings and restart the engine when requested.

support.title: Transcripts and exports
paragraphs: Review speaker labels and source timestamps before relying on generated text. Select an export format and save location.

support.title: Desktop and server storage
paragraphs: Desktop mode uses local SQLite and file storage. A separately deployed server uses its configured database and object store, so storage and access depend on that deployment.

privacy.title: Media and derived data
paragraphs: Desktop processing stores imported media, playback files, transcripts, summaries, vectors and conversations in application data. Server deployments store these using their configured infrastructure.

privacy.title: Remote imports
paragraphs: Podcast resolution and media downloads contact directory, feed, transcript and media hosts. Those hosts receive the network requests needed for the import.

privacy.title: AI providers
paragraphs: Configured transcription services can receive audio. Embedding and language-model services receive relevant transcript text, questions and context. Endpoints can be local or remote; local desktop packaging does not make remote AI processing local.

privacy.title: Credentials
paragraphs: Desktop provider settings, including supplied credentials, are saved in a local settings file with platform permission handling. They are not described as encrypted storage. Codex CLI mode uses the CLI authentication configured on the machine.

privacy.title: Connected clients
paragraphs: Optional MCP access exposes supported episode tools to connected clients. Content returned to a client is then subject to that client and any AI services it uses.

privacy.title: Exports and removal
paragraphs: Exported transcripts and summaries remain in the selected destination. To remove the desktop library, quit the application and remove its application data after preserving anything needed; exported copies and remotely processed data require separate handling.

privacy.title: Diagnostics
paragraphs: The inspected application has operational logs but no integrated analytics or crash-reporting service was found. Review logs and exported content before sharing them for support.
